verdict.label: HOLD — Morning call confirmed; NVDA binary defines Thursday's open
verdict.rationale_short: The morning HOLD was correct: Wednesday's tape delivered the base case, not the bear case. Yields eased modestly (30Y to ~5.14% from 5.20%; 10Y to 4.66% from 4.70%), VIX retreated to 17.96 below the 18 bearish threshold, and SPX held near Tuesday's close. Regime is not resolved — 30Y remains 114bps above the 5.0% trigger — but the directional drift is the first positive since May 14. NVDA Q1 FY2027 results released after the close are the sole binary determining Thursday's setup: a strong Q2 guide (>$87B) upgrades the call; a light guide reinstates Step Aside.

bear_case: The NVDA earnings result is the one catalyst capable of resolving this week's regime question in hours. An in-line or disappointing Q2 guide would confirm that the AI capex cycle is maturing — the exact thesis that broke the tape May 14-15. With the 30Y at 5.14% and the Warsh rate-hike narrative active, a semis disappointment is the setup for a break below SPX 7,320 and a formal Step Aside call. The CNN Fear & Greed index at 60.29 means retail has not capitulated and is still buying the dip — meaning there is dry powder for one more leg lower if NVDA's forward guide disappoints. If NVDA guides Q2 below $86B and SPX closes below 7,320 on Thursday, the HOLD is too generous and Step Aside is the correct overnight downgrade.
